one_line_contribution: A label-free routing rule for distilled agent experience: an item belongs in the always-on instruction rather than the retrieval bank in proportion to its coverage breadth (the fraction of unlabeled deployment queries for which it enters top-k), and the payoff of promotion is the top-k slot it vacates rather than the text it adds - the latter isolated by refill / no-refill / padding controls at k=2.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, one conceded and one not. Conceded: MemGPT/A-MEM-style capacity paging plus OS-flavoured hot/warm/cold agent-memory tiering (the 2025 MemoryOS-type line), which already promotes by access heat into an always-resident tier, and working-set estimation, which already says estimate future access from a representative recent window rather than stale logs. The proposal's stated differentiators (tiers are not latency-equivalent, the competitive tier is always exactly full, the payoff is the vacated slot) are real and the refill/no-refill/padding controls are a genuinely unrun experiment, so this is a narrowing rather than a kill. Not conceded, and more damaging: the in-context-example selection literature, which has scored candidate exemplars by coverage over an *unlabeled* target pool for years - vote-k selective annotation (Su et al., ICLR 2023) picks a representative subset by graph coverage of unlabeled deployment queries with zero labels, and DPP/CEIL-style diversity selection exists precisely because redundant broad exemplars crowd out complementary ones. b(m) is also, mechanically, a retrieval hubness score: hubs that appear in many top-k lists, and demoting them (mutual proximity, local scaling, CSLS, MMR) is a known and cheaper intervention that needs no instruction tier at all. That b(m) is simultaneously a hubness statistic and a coverage statistic is never acknowledged, and it means the proposal has an untested rival explanation and an untested cheaper fix.
strongest_objection: The two headline contrasts are decided by measurement budget and by an absent comparator, not by the theory. (1) P4 asks breadth routing to beat utility routing by >=3 EM, but u(m) is estimated from 6 probes on each of 60 items. A per-item paired estimate at n=6 has a standard error on the order of 15-20 EM points; utility routing is therefore a random permutation of the top-60 items with a faint signal, and b(m) is computed on 500 queries with no sampling noise at all. Breadth will beat utility at that budget even if utility is the true causal variable, so P4's central comparison cannot distinguish the hypothesis from estimator noise. Worse, arm E2 (iv) pure playbook is built by merging the *highest-utility* items, so the same 6-probe noise handicaps the playbook baseline that P2 must beat by >=3 points - the two thresholds that would be reported as the paper's result are both partly artifacts of how little was spent estimating the rival statistic. (2) P2 never requires the breadth hybrid to beat E2 (i) no-memory. The track's own starting position is that this bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven, and that write-path repairs neutralized harm without converting it to gain; E0's gate explicitly passes when the bank matters in the harmful direction. So the fully satisfying outcome - hybrid beats top-k by 3, beats playbook by 3, beats MemGPT-style promotion by 3 - is compatible with every memory arm sitting below the no-memory arm, i.e. with the recommended system being worse than deleting the memory subsystem. A hybrid that wins only by injecting less of a harmful bank is a volume result, which the pilot already established, not a placement law. Secondary but sharp: E1's 75/75 stratification equalizes bank-side availability across items by construction, which removes the main channel through which breadth is supposed to act and makes the regressed A(m) not the deployment placement advantage; and the tested quantity is an item-level fixed effect estimated from 14 items with four item-level predictors, from which P4 additionally asserts a null (utility and frequency not significant after conditioning on breadth). An absence-of-effect claim from 14 items is uninterpretable, and the likeliest confound - breadth correlates with item abstractness, so general strategy text belongs in an instruction for reasons that have nothing to do with slot economics - is controlled only for item length.
what_would_fix_it: Five changes, all inside the stated envelope. (1) Equalize the routing-statistic budget: either give utility a fair estimate (30+ probes on fewer items, or a shrinkage/hierarchical estimate with reported reliability) or, better, degrade breadth to the same information budget by recomputing b(m) from a 6-query subsample and showing breadth still wins - and report the split-half reliability of b, u and f, since no comparison of routing variables is interpretable without it. Route the pure-playbook arm by something other than the noisy u as well, or report it under both selection rules. (2) Pre-register hybrid vs no-memory at the same >=3-point bar, put no-memory on every accuracy-versus-token curve, and state explicitly that no headline is claimed if no-memory is the best arm. (3) Add the missing E1 cell (d): item in the instruction AND retained in the bank. Cells (a) instruction-only, (b) bank-only, (c) absent and (d) both give a clean item-level decomposition of availability versus slot-vacating, and (d) is the cheapest possible direct test of the inverted-caching claim - far cheaper than resting the mechanism entirely on the admittedly underpowered k=2 refill/no-refill contrast. Replace the 75/75 stratification with deployment-proportional sampling plus inverse-probability weights so A(m) estimates the quantity the theory is about. (4) Add MMR / hubness-corrected retrieval (below). (5) Expand E1 to at least 30 items or delete every null claim about u and f. Finally, the search log promised in the Commitment section has to be run before, not after, the design is frozen, because a collision would change which arms matter.
missing_baseline: Diversity- or hubness-corrected top-k retrieval at identical k and identical tokens - MMR re-ranking, or a hub-demotion score such as mutual proximity / local scaling / CSLS applied to the same bge-large index. This is the baseline that most directly threatens the paper: it removes broad items from the competitive tier on a per-query basis, frees exactly the slots the hybrid claims credit for, requires no instruction tier, no consolidation, no LLM merge and no calibration labels, and it is what a retrieval person would reach for on being told that a few items enter almost every top-k list. If MMR captures most of the hybrid's margin, the contribution collapses to a retrieval-normalization result. Also omitted: the E1 (d) cell (item in instruction and left in bank), which isolates slot-vacating from availability at item level; a bank-deduplication / near-duplicate-merge control, since broad items are plausibly near-duplicates and drop-only does not separate deduplication from breadth; and a per-query oracle-k arm. Separately, the MIPROv2 arm (E2 vii) is capped at 400 rollouts, which is well under what MIPROv2 normally needs to converge on a multi-hop ReAct program, so as specified it is a weakened baseline rather than an honest test of instruction+demonstration coupling; the cap needs justification or a convergence curve.
preprint_collision: This is the weakest possible collision check: zero searches were run, every web-search invocation failed, and the closest-work list is explicitly recollection. The proposal deserves credit for saying so plainly rather than dressing up a stale list, and for converting MemGPT-style usage promotion from foil into a first-class arm - but candour does not substitute for a search, and by the standard that novelty must be established rather than asserted, this proposal has not established it. The tool failure is also not a complete excuse: the omissions I consider most damaging (vote-k / selective-annotation coverage selection over unlabeled pools, DPP-diversity exemplar selection, and the retrieval hubness literature) are indexed, years-old work that a recollection-based list should have surfaced, so the gap is substantive and not merely unverified. On live preprint risk, the proposal names the right danger zone and I share its assessment: the mid-2025-onward context-engineering / agent-memory-tiering line (ACE-style playbooks, ReasoningBank-style banks, OS-style tiered memory with heat-based promotion, context-budget allocation papers) is exactly where a hot/cold promotion or instruction-versus-retrieval budget allocation paper would land, and I cannot rule out that such a preprint already exists; what I would expect it *not* to contain is the refill/no-refill/padding triad and the threshold-retrieval difference-of-differences, which is the correct fallback the proposal identifies. Recommendation: the dated search log promised in the Commitment section should be a precondition for this proposal advancing, not a pre-submission chore, and it should be extended to cover exemplar-coverage selection and hubness, which the current framing does not know it needs to search for.
